question.problem:
Two fair  four-sided dice are rolled and $X$ is the absolute difference of their scores. The probability mass function $f(x)$ of $X$ is shown in the table below. What is $\text{SD}[X]?$ 

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{3}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ |
question.worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a random variable $X$ is defined as

$$
\text{SD}[X]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]},
$$

where the variance can be computed using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

First, we need to compute $\text{E}[X].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =0\cdot f(0)+1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3) \\  & =0(\frac{1}{4})+1(\frac{3}{8})+2(\frac{1}{4})+3(\frac{1}{8}) \\  & =\frac{5}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={0}^{2}\cdot f(0)+{1}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2)+{3}^{2}\cdot f(3) \\  & =0(\frac{1}{4})+1(\frac{3}{8})+4(\frac{1}{4})+9(\frac{1}{8}) \\  & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}-{(\frac{5}{4})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}-\frac{25}{16} \\  & =\frac{15}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{SD}[X] & =\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{15}{16}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{15}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
